text:
morgan: :warning: Autoscaler not adding GPU nodes in us-west-2 after sudden traffic spike, ~120 pending pods with gpu requests. latency alarm on inference-prod.
alex: seeing same, HPA shows desired=0->10 but nodes stay at 3. pods Pending -> InsufficientGPUs.
priya: autoscaler-bot alerted scale-up_started at 1729005100 then scale_down at 1729005300? looks like thrash.
autoscaler-bot: [alert] ClusterAutoscaler: scaleUp failed for 5m; reason: FailedGetResourceQuota (quota exhausted in us-west-2), lastErr: allocation timed out
sam: can someone paste `kubectl describe hpa -n infra inference-service` and `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep Pending`? we need root cause: metric signal or cloud quota.
julia: paste from HPA: "Metrics unavailable: failed to get metrics from custom-metrics: dial tcp 10.4.2.11:8080: connect: connection refused" — metric-adapter seems flapping.
alex: aha, metric-adapter restart loop on node gpu-ctrl-1. logs show OOMKilled on adapter exporter after memory spike.
priya: so CA is getting stale/missing metrics -> decides no scale up or performs conservative oscillating decisions.
morgan: impact: inference tail latency > 2s, some requests 503. Traffic currently at 3x baseline due to campaign. We should mitigate immediately: manual scale + route shift.
sam: mitigation plan:
- step1: manually add 4 GPU instances in us-west-2 pool (temp) — alex to run.
- step2: cordon gpu-ctrl-1 and force restart metric-adapter; disable autoscaler scale-down for 15m.
- step3: if provisioning fails due to cloud quota, shift traffic for low-priority routes to us-east-1 and reduce batch size.
alex: starting manual instance creation: `gcloud compute instances create inference-gpu-ephemeral-1 --zone=us-west2-a --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1` (running now)
deploy-bot: deploy request to inference-service v2.3.1 queued — no change to current replicas.
priya: temporarily patch HPA to use external queue-length metric as fallback: `kubectl patch hpa inference-service -p '{"spec":{"metrics":[{"type":"External","external":{"metric":{"name":"inference_queue_length"},"target":{"type":"AverageValue","averageValue":"10"}}}]}}'`
julia: also increasing CA `--scale-down-delay` and `--expander=least-waste` won't hurt; I'll apply a conservative flag.
alex: instances created but reporting quotas: cloud API returns QuotaExceeded for GPUs in us-west2-b; created in us-west2-a succeeded. nodes joined, pods scheduled -> Pending count dropping.
morgan: monitoring: tail latency down to 700ms, pending pods from 120 -> 30 in 6m.
sam: root cause summary so far: metric-adapter OOM caused missing custom metrics -> CA made no/incorrect choices; secondarily cloud GPU quota fragmentation caused some zones to fail allocation leading to partial scale-ups and perceived thrash.
priya: action items:
- short-term: increase metric-adapter memory limit and restart (priya)
- short-term: set CA fallback to use pending pod count if metrics unavailable (sam)
- mid-term: implement cross-zone quota failover and add capacity reservation for spikes (morgan + infra)
- postmortem: include runbook updates for manual add and traffic shift, and cost review for ephemeral GPU spins (julia)
julia: I'm going to file a ticket for quota increase with cloud account and tag billing for ephemeral usage during incident.
alex: metric-adapter memory bump applied, adapter now stable. CA logs show scaleUp accepted. autoscaler-bot: scaleUp completed at 1729006001, added 5 nodes.
morgan: removing cordon from gpu-ctrl-1 and re-enabling autoscaler scale-down. continuing to watch for 30m.
priya: i'll open a postmortem draft after monitoring window. initial blameless note: metric-adapter memory leak + quota fragmentation + spike load.
sam: thanks team. please add any missed notes in the thread. :thumbsup:
